CLASS 28 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Phonics & Beginning Sounds

Age 4–5 YearsClass 28 of 28Adventures 24 sound gamesSubjects Sounds · rhymes · words

Phonics is listening made visible: this class plays with the sounds inside words — first sounds, ending sounds, rhymes, syllables and the tiny vowels that hide in the middle. Twenty-four draw-on-the-picture adventures, each with a printable worksheet in the Phonics worksheet library.

Every game speaks: words and pure letter sounds play out loud, with replay and a mute switch. No reading required — ears lead, letters follow.

Meet the adventures ↓Grown-up nearby for the first round makes everything smoother.
TODAY’S CLASS

How this class works.

Phonics asks a new kind of listening: not what a word means, but what it is MADE of. The class walks up a gentle slope — hear a sound, find it in pictures, hear it at the start or end of words, blend sounds into words, swap sounds to make new words, and finally count the invisible sounds inside what you hear.

  1. 1 Warm-up: the first-sound games
  2. 2 Rhymes and blending
  3. 3 Two or three adventures from the shelves
  4. 4 The matching worksheet, printed
  5. 5 Class complete

Teach the letter sounds, one lesson at a time.

Twenty-six letter-sound lessons, Aa apple to Zz zebra. Every lesson is right here on this page — the original flashcard beside the step-by-step teaching: how the sound is really made, the words to say, and one game that drills it. Five minutes a letter, in any order your child points at.

Aa — AppleBb — BallCc — CatDd — DogEe — ElephantFf — FishGg — GoatHh — HatIi — IglooJj — JamKk — KiteLl — LionMm — MoonNn — NestOo — OctopusPp — PigQq — QueenRr — RabbitSs — SunTt — TurtleUu — UmbrellaVv — VanWw — WhaleXx — XylophoneYy — Yo-YoZz — Zebra

Every lesson pairs with a printable card in the A–Z letter-sound flashcard set, and the sounds keep drilling in the adventures above.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Sound play in the kitchen and the car.

I spy, with my little ear

  • “I spy something that starts with sss…” — soap, sock, spoon. Ears only, no letters needed.
  • Swap roles and let your child be the spy.

Stretched-word soup

  • Say a word stretched out — “mmmuuunnnch” — and let your child squash it back together.
  • Silly voices welcome; the stretching is the point.

Rhyme sandwiches

  • Any rhyme pair becomes a sandwich: “cat-hat sandwich, please!”
  • Make the order, serve it, giggle, repeat.

Phonics rewards tiny sessions. Five minutes of sound play, done warmly, beats thirty done tired.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Phonics has one famous rule: sounds first, letter names second. The letter is “em” but the sound is “mmm” — and children who learn the sound first learn to read with less un-learning. Every game here plays real recordings of both words and pure sounds; press replay as often as needed, and say the sounds with your child so the ears have company.

The printable worksheets are built to work without any audio: every sheet tells you exactly what to say and includes a grown-up answer line. Browse the phonics worksheets and print the twin of whichever game your child loved.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 26 cards in Phonics & Beginning Sounds, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Phonics & Beginning Sounds. We have 26 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Apple

    “A says a — a — apple. Say it slowly, then quickly, then let your child finish the word on their own.”

    How: Line up three things that start with a — an apple, an ant toy, the letter A from the fridge magnets — and say each one with the same big open mouth.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Ball

    “B says b — b — ball. Press your lips together, pop them open and hum: b-b-ball.”

    How: Bounce a ball and say one b-word per bounce — ball, bounce, big, blue. Falling over the words is allowed; bouncing without talking is not.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Cat

    “C says c — c — cat. A short clicking sound at the back of the mouth, then the word: cat.”

    How: Go on a c-hunt around the home: cup, coat, carrot, cat (if you have one — a toy cat counts). Line the finds up and say each with the click.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Dog

    “D says d — d — dog. Tap the tongue just behind the top teeth and let it bounce: d-d-dog.”

    How: Play the drum: d is a tapping sound, so tap the table like a drum — d-d-d-dog — then switch: one tap for d, two taps for dog.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Elephant

    “E says e — e — elephant. A short ‘eh‘ like a tiny echo, then the whole word: elephant.”

    How: Elephant walk with sound: swing one arm like a trunk and trumpet “eh-eh-eh” across the room, then stop at three e-things you can find or name — egg, elf, elephant.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Fish

    “F says f — f — fish. Top teeth on the bottom lip and blow: f-f-fish.”

    How: Feather race: put a feather or a scrap of tissue on the table and blow it along with f-f-f sounds. The sound that moves the feather is the right one.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Goat

    “G says g — g — goat. A growly sound from the back, then the word: goat.”

    How: Glug like a bottle: tip your head back and make three glug-glug sounds, then say g-words in the same throaty voice — goat, gum, go.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Hat

    “H says h — h — hat. A soft puff of air like warming your hands, then the word: hat.”

    How: Steam game: hold a hand in front of the mouth and send three h-puffs onto it — h-h-hat. Warm hands with h-breaths, then say all the h-words you know.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Igloo

    “I says i — i — igloo. A short ‘ih‘, quick and light, then the word: igloo.”

    How: Inchworm game: crawl one tiny “inch” per i-word — igloo, insect, ink, it. Small sound, small moves: short /i/ is the tiniest vowel in the set.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Jam

    “J says j — j — jam. Tongue up, then a small jump: j-j-jam.”

    How: Jam-toast letters: spread jam on toast, draw the letter J in it with a spoon, lick the spoon and say three j-words — jam, jump, juice.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Kite

    “K says k — k — kite. A clean click at the back of the mouth, then let the word fly: kite.”

    How: Fly an imaginary kite on a string: tug the string for every k-word — kite, kick, key, kiss. Four tugs, four words, one very tiring arm.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Lion

    “L says l — l — lion. Tongue tip up behind the teeth and let it sing: l-l-lion.”

    How: Trace a big l in the air with one finger while the tongue tip stays pointed up — then draw a giant l on paper and roar one soft lion roar on every corner.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Moon

    “M says m — m — moon. Press your lips together and hum: mmmmoon.”

    How: The long hum: hold m for as long as one breath — mmmmm — then land it on a word: moon. Three landings, three m-words, one dizzy child.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Nest

    “N says n — n — nest. Tongue up behind the teeth and hum through the nose: nnnest.”

    How: Nose-hum check: pinch the nose gently while humming n — the buzz stops. Let go, buzz returns. Then say n-words: nest, nose, nine.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Octopus

    “O says o — o — octopus. Round the mouth like the letter itself, then say: octopus.”

    How: Round-mouth contest: say o-words while holding an O shape with your lips — octopus, on, off, ox. Whoever breaks the circle first loses the round.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Pig

    “P says p — p — pig. Lips together, then a small puff: p-p-pig.”

    How: Tissue test: hold a tissue in front of the mouth and say p — the tissue jumps. Then say b — it stays. One game, both twins, sorted.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Queen

    “Q says kw — kw — queen. A /k/ click straight into a puff of wind, then the word: queen.”

    How: Cough-into-blow: make the k click, then blow out like blowing candles — k-wuh. Repeat three times and land it on queen. The two sounds are one team.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Rabbit

    “R says r — r — rabbit. Curl the tongue up but let it touch nothing: r-r-rabbit.”

    How: Growl like a tiger then say r-words — r-r-rabbit, r-r-run. The growl puts the tongue in exactly the right curled place without any explaining.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Sun

    “S says s — s — sun. A long hiss like a snake, then the word: sun.”

    How: Snake race: hiss s for as long as one breath, then land it on an s-word — ssssun. Hiss three times, three s-words, one medal for the longest hiss.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Turtle

    “T says t — t — turtle. Tap the tongue behind the teeth, quick and quiet: t-t-turtle.”

    How: Tick-tock tongue: tap the tongue like a clock — t-t-t-t — then land it on t-words: turtle, toe, tea. Fast taps, slow words, one careful tongue.

  24. Cards 21–26
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Umbrella

    “U says u — u — umbrella. A relaxed ‘uh‘, the sound the mouth makes when nothing is trying, then: umbrella.”

    How: Up-and-under game: jump up on one u-word, duck under the table on another — up! under! umbrella! Three rounds and the vowel is drilled for the day.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Van

    “V says v — v — van. Top teeth on the bottom lip and buzz: v-v-van.”

    How: Vibration check: hand on the throat while saying v — the buzz is on. Then say f — the buzz stops. Same teeth, different switch.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Whale

    “W says w — w — whale. Round the lips small, then open into the word: whale.”

    How: Spout game: hands together like a spout, whoosh up on each w-word — whale, water, wave, windy. The whoosh is the glide the lips are making.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Xylophone

    “X says z here — xylophone starts with a /z/ sound. But x’s day job is the /ks/ at the end: box, fox, six.”

    How: End-of-word hunt: say box, fox, six, mix and listen for the /ks/ at the finish — then knock pretend xylophone bars: x is the sound of the ending.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Yo-Yo

    “Y says y — y — yo-yo. A quick glide off the tongue, twice, because the word says itself twice: yo-yo.”

    How: Yo-yo hands: fist up, fist down on each syllable — yo, yo — then swap in other y-words: yes, yell, you. Two syllables, two fists, endless fun.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Zebra

    “Z says z — z — zebra. A buzzing bee sound, then the word: zebra.”

    How: Bee-hunt: buzz z around the room like a bee looking for flowers, landing on z-words — zebra, zoo, zip. When the bee lands, the word gets said.

  31. 28
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  32. 29
    Check

    “Can you find Apple? Now show me Nest.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  33. 30
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 26 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
